By his inward working he will deliver us from being “unstable as water,” and cause us to be rooted and grounded. It is part of the way he saves us — this building us up into Christ Jesus and causing us to abide in him. Dear reader, you may look for this every day; and you will not be disappointed. He whom you trust will make you like a tree planted by streams of water, kept so well that even your leaf will not wither.

What a strength a confirmed Christian is to a church! He is a comfort to the sorrowful, and a help to the weak. Would you not like to be one? Confirmed believers are pillars in the house of our God. They are not carried away by every wind of doctrine, nor overthrown by sudden temptation. They are a great stay to others, and act as anchors in times of trouble in the church. You who are beginning the holy life hardly dare to hope that you will become like them. But you need not fear; the good Lord will work in you as well as in them. One of these days you who are now a babe in Christ will be a father in the church. Hope for this great thing; but hope for it as a gift of grace, and not as the wages of work, or as the product of your own energy.

The inspired apostle Paul speaks of these people as to be confirmed to the end. He expected the grace of God to preserve them personally to the end of their lives, or till the Lord Jesus came. Indeed, he expected that the whole church of God in every place and in all time would be kept to the end of this age, till the Lord Jesus as the Bridegroom comes to celebrate the wedding feast with his perfected Bride. All who are in Christ will be confirmed in him till that glorious day. Has he not said, “Because I live, you+ also will live”? He also said, “I give My sheep eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.” He who has begun a good work in you+ will confirm it until the day of Christ. The work of grace in the soul is not a surface reformation; the life planted in the new birth comes from a living and incorruptible seed, which lives and abides forever; and God’s promises to believers are not of a passing kind, but their fulfillment includes the believer’s holding to his way till he comes to endless glory. We are kept by the power of God, through faith, to salvation. “The righteous will hold to his way.” Not as the result of our own merit or strength, but as a gift of free and undeserved favor, those who believe are “kept in Jesus Christ.” Of the sheep of his fold Jesus will lose none; no member of his body will die; no gem of his treasure will be missing on the day when he gathers up his jewels. Dear reader, the salvation which is received by faith is not a thing of months and years; for our Lord Jesus has “obtained eternal salvation for us,” and what is eternal cannot come to an end.

Paul also declares his expectation that the Corinthian saints would be “confirmed to the end, blameless.” This blamelessness is a precious part of our keeping. To be kept holy is better than merely to be kept safe. It is a dreadful thing when you see religious people blundering from one disgrace into another; they have not believed in the power of our Lord to make them blameless. The lives of some professing Christians are a series of stumbles; they are never quite down, and yet they are seldom steady on their feet. This is not fitting for a believer; he is invited to walk with God, and by faith he can attain steady perseverance in holiness; and he ought to do so. The Lord is able not only to save us from hell, but to keep us from falling. We need not yield to temptation. Is it not written, “Sin shall not have dominion over you+”? The Lord is able to keep the feet of his saints; and he will do it if we will trust him to do so. We need not defile our garments; by his grace we may keep them unstained by the world; we are bound to do this, “for without holiness no one will see the Lord.”

The apostle prophesied for these believers what he would have us seek — that we may be preserved “blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Our Revised Version has “unreproveable,” instead of “blameless.” Possibly a better rendering would be “unimpeachable.” God grant that on that last great day we may stand free from every charge, so that no one in the whole universe may dare to challenge our claim to be the redeemed of the Lord. We have sins and weaknesses to mourn over, but these are not the kind of faults which would prove us to be outside of Christ; we will be clear of hypocrisy, deceit, hatred, and delight in sin; for these things would be fatal charges. Despite our failings, the Holy Spirit can work in us a character spotless before men; so that, like Daniel, we will give accusing tongues no grounds, except in the matter of our religion. Multitudes of godly men and women have shown lives so transparent, so consistent throughout, that no one could gainsay them. The Lord will be able to say of many a believer, as he did of Job when Satan stood before him, “Have you considered My servant, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil?” This is what my reader must aim at, and look for at the Lord’s hands. This is the triumph of the saints — to keep following the Lamb wherever he goes, maintaining our integrity as before the living God. May we never turn aside into crooked ways, and give the adversary cause to blaspheme. Of the true believer it is written, “He keeps himself, and the evil one does not touch him.” May it be written so of us!

Friend, you who are just beginning in the divine life, the Lord can give you an irreproachable character. Even though in your past life you may have gone far into sin, the Lord can completely deliver you from the power of former habit, and make you an example of virtue. He can not only make you moral, but he can make you abhor every false way and follow after all that is saintly. Do not doubt it. The chief of sinners need not fall one bit behind the purest of the saints. Believe for this, and according to your faith it will be done to you.

Oh, what a joy it will be to be found blameless in the day of judgment! We are not wrong to join in singing that charming hymn:

““Bold shall I stand in that great day,

For who aught to my charge shall lay;

While through thy blood absolved I am,

From sin’s tremendous curse and shame?””

What bliss it will be to enjoy that dauntless courage, when heaven and earth flee away from the face of the Judge of all! This bliss will be the portion of everyone who looks only to the grace of God in Christ Jesus, and in that sacred strength wages continual war with all sin.

Why Saints Persevere

The hope which filled Paul’s heart for the Corinthian brethren is, as we have already seen, full of comfort to those who tremble about their future. But why did he believe that the brethren would be confirmed to the end?

I want you to notice that he gives his reasons. Here they are:

““God is faithful, by whom you+ were called into the fellowship of His Son Jesus Christ.” — 1 Cor 1:9.”

The apostle does not say, “You+ are faithful.” Alas! the faithfulness of man is a very unreliable thing; it is mere vanity. He does not say, “You+ have faithful ministers to lead and guide you+, and so I trust you+ will be safe.” Oh, no! if we are kept by men, we will be poorly kept. He puts it, “God is faithful.” If we are found faithful, it will be because God is faithful. On the faithfulness of our covenant God the whole weight of our salvation must rest. On this glorious attribute of God the matter hinges. We are as changeable as the wind, as frail as a spider’s web, as weak as water. No reliance can be placed on our natural qualities, or our spiritual attainments; but God remains faithful. He is faithful in his love; he knows no change, nor shadow of turning. He is faithful to his purpose; he does not begin a work and then leave it undone. He is faithful to his relationships; as a Father he will not disown his children, as a friend he will not deny his people, as a Creator he will not forsake the work of his own hands. He is faithful to his promises, and will never allow one of them to fail a single believer. He is faithful to his covenant, which he has made with us in Christ Jesus, and ratified with the blood of his sacrifice. He is faithful to his Son, and will not allow his precious blood to be spilled in vain. He is faithful to his people, to whom he has promised eternal life, and from whom he will not turn away.

This faithfulness of God is the foundation and cornerstone of our hope of final perseverance. The saints will persevere in holiness, because God perseveres in grace. He perseveres in blessing, and so believers persevere in being blessed. He continues to keep his people, and so they continue to keep his commandments. This is good solid ground to rest on, and it fits delightfully with the motto of this little book, “all of grace.” So it is free favor and infinite mercy which ring in the dawn of salvation, and the same sweet bells ring out melodiously through the whole day of grace.

You see that the only reasons for hoping that we will be confirmed to the end, and be found blameless at the last, are found in our God; but in him these reasons are exceedingly abundant.

They lie first in what God has done. He has gone so far in blessing us that he cannot possibly turn back. Paul reminds us that he has “called us into the fellowship of His Son Jesus Christ.” Has he called us? Then the call cannot be reversed; for “God’s gifts and His call are without repentance.” The Lord never turns back from the effectual call of his grace. “Those He called, He also justified; those He justified, He also glorified”: this is the unvarying rule of God’s way of working. There is a common call, of which it is said, “Many are called, but few are chosen”; but the call we are now thinking of is another kind, which signals special love, and makes it certain that we will possess what we are called to. In such a case it is with the one called just as with Abraham’s seed, of whom the Lord said, “I have called you from the ends of the earth, and said to you, ‘You are My servant’; I have chosen you and not rejected you.”

In what the Lord has done we see strong reasons for our preservation and future glory, because the Lord has called us into the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ. It means into partnership with Jesus Christ, and I want you to consider carefully what this means. If you really are called by divine grace, you have come into fellowship with the Lord Jesus Christ, so as to be joint owner with him in all things. From now on you are one with him in the sight of the Most High. The Lord Jesus bore your sins in his own body on the tree, being made a curse for you; and at the same time he has become your righteousness, so that you are justified in him. You are Christ’s, and Christ is yours. As Adam stood for his descendants, so Jesus stands for all who are in him. As husband and wife are one, so Jesus is one with all those who are united to him by faith; one by a marriage union which can never be broken. More than this, believers are members of the body of Christ, and so are one with him by a loving, living, lasting union. God has called us into this union, this fellowship, this partnership, and by this very fact he has given us the token and pledge that we will be confirmed to the end. If we were considered apart from Christ, we would be poor perishable units, soon dissolved and carried away to destruction; but as one with Jesus we are made partakers of his nature, and are endowed with his immortal life. Our destiny is linked with that of our Lord, and until he can be destroyed it is not possible that we should perish.

Dwell much on this partnership with the Son of God, to which you have been called: for all your hope lies there. You can never be poor while Jesus is rich, since you are in one firm with him. Need can never overtake you, since you are joint owner with him who is Possessor of heaven and earth. You can never fail; for though one of the partners in the firm is as poor as a church mouse, and in himself an utter bankrupt, who could not pay half a cent on the dollar of his heavy debts, yet the other partner is inconceivably, inexhaustibly rich. In such a partnership you are raised above the depression of the times, the changes of the future, and the shock of the end of all things. The Lord has called you into the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ, and by that act and deed he has put you in a place of unfailing safety.

If you really are a believer, you are one with Jesus, and therefore you are secure. Do you not see that it must be so? You must be confirmed to the end, until the day of his appearing, if you have indeed been made one with Jesus by the irrevocable act of God. Christ and the believing sinner are in the same boat: unless Jesus sinks, the believer will never drown. Jesus has taken his redeemed into such union with himself that he must first be struck down, overcome, and dishonored, before the least of those he purchased can be harmed. His name is at the head of the firm, and until it can be dishonored we are secure against all dread of failure.

So then, with the utmost confidence let us go forward into the unknown future, linked eternally with Jesus. If the men of the world cry, “Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her Beloved?” we will joyfully confess that we do lean on Jesus, and that we mean to lean on him more and more. Our faithful God is an ever-flowing well of delight, and our fellowship with the Son of God is a full river of joy. Knowing these glorious things, we cannot be discouraged: no, rather we cry with the apostle, “Who shall separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord?”

Close

If my reader has not followed me step by step as he has read my pages, I am truly sorry. Reading books is of little value unless the truths which pass before the mind are grasped, made one’s own, and carried out in practice. It is as if someone saw plenty of food in a shop and yet stayed hungry, for lack of eating any of it himself. It is all in vain, dear reader, that you and I have met, unless you have actually taken hold of Christ Jesus, my Lord. On my part there was a clear desire to do you good, and I have done my best to that end. It pains me that I have not been able to do you good, for I have longed to win that privilege. I was thinking of you when I wrote this page, and I laid down my pen and solemnly knelt in prayer for everyone who would read it. It is my firm conviction that great numbers of readers will receive a blessing, even though you refuse to be one of them. But why should you refuse? If you do not desire the choice blessing which I wanted to bring you, at least do me the justice of admitting that the blame for your final doom will not lie at my door. When we two meet before the great white throne, you will not be able to charge me with having idly used the attention which you were kind enough to give me while you were reading my little book. God knows I wrote each line for your eternal good. I now in spirit take you by the hand. I give you a firm grip. Do you feel my brotherly grasp? The tears are in my eyes as I look at you and say, Why will you die? Will you not give your soul a thought? Will you perish through sheer carelessness? Oh, do not do so; but weigh these solemn matters, and make sure of eternity. Do not refuse Jesus, his love, his blood, his salvation. Why should you do so? Can you do it?

I beg you,

Do not turn away from your Redeemer!

If, on the other hand, my prayers are heard, and you, my reader, have been led to trust the Lord Jesus and receive salvation by grace from him, then hold always to this doctrine, and this way of living. Let Jesus be your all in all, and let free grace be the one line in which you live and move. There is no life like that of one who lives in the favor of God. To receive everything as a free gift keeps the mind from self-righteous pride, and from self-accusing despair. It makes the heart grow warm with grateful love, and so it creates a feeling in the soul which is infinitely more acceptable to God than anything that can possibly come from slavish fear. Those who hope to be saved by trying to do their best know nothing of that glowing fervor, that holy warmth, that devout joy in God, which come with salvation freely given according to the grace of God. The slavish spirit of self-salvation is no match for the joyous spirit of adoption. There is more real worth in the slightest stirring of faith than in all the tugging of bond-slaves to the law, or all the weary machinery of devotees who would climb to heaven by rounds of ceremonies. Faith is spiritual, and God, who is a spirit, delights in it for that reason. Years of saying prayers, and church-going or chapel-going, and ceremonies, and performances, may be only an abomination in the sight of the spiritual Jehovah; but a glance from the eye of true faith is spiritual, and so it is dear to him. “The Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.” Look first to the inner man, and to the spiritual part of religion, and the rest will then follow in due course.

If you are saved yourself, be on the watch for the souls of others. Your own heart will not prosper unless it is filled with intense concern to bless your fellow men. The life of your soul lies in faith; its health lies in love. He who does not long to lead others to Jesus has never been under the spell of love himself. Get to the work of the Lord — the work of love. Begin at home. Visit your neighbors next. Bring light to the village, or the street where you live. Scatter the word of the Lord wherever your hand can reach.

If those who are converted become winners of others, who knows what may spring from my little book? Already I begin praising God for the conversions which he will work by it, and by those whom it leads to Jesus. Probably most of the results will come when my right hand, which is now leaving its mark on the page, lies paralyzed in death.

Reader, meet me in heaven! Do not go down to hell. There is no coming back from that place of misery. Why do you want to enter the way of death when heaven’s gate is open before you? Do not refuse the free pardon, the full salvation which Jesus grants to all who trust him. Do not hesitate and delay. You have had enough of resolving; come to action. Believe in Jesus now, with full and immediate decision. Take words with you and come to your Lord today, this very day. Remember, O soul, it may be

now or never

with you. Let it be now; it would be horrible if it were never.

Farewell. Again I charge you,

meet me in heaven.
